The URLs are constructed using standard parameter expansion and do not involve command substitution or dynamic evaluation that could lead to code execution during sourcing.

The file contains no top-level commands, command substitutions, or function calls outside of standard packaging variables and the `package()` function. The `pkgver` is hardcoded, so no execution occurs to determine the version. As a result, sourcing this PKGBUILD during `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` will not execute any unexpected or malicious code.

All checksums are provided via sha512sums (not skipped), and while their presence isn't required for safety in this gate, it reinforces source integrity. No network operations or file modifications occur at parse time. Therefore, fetching and parsing this PKGBUILD is safe under the current narrow scope.
</details>

The sources are downloaded as prebuilt binaries for multiple architectures (x86_64, armv6h, aarch64), and each has corresponding SHA-512 checksums provided, ensuring integrity verification during package building.

The `package()` function performs a straightforward installation of the `shellcheck` binary into `/usr/bin`, using standard `install` commands with proper permissions (`755`). There are no suspicious operations such as network requests at build time, obfuscated code, or execution of downloaded content beyond extraction. The use of `${pkgname%-bin}` for string manipulation is standard Bash syntax in PKGBUILDs and serves to derive the correct upstream binary name (`shellcheck`) from the package name (`shellcheck-bin`).

No conflicts with packaging best practices were found. While the checksums are specified and not marked as 'SKIP', they are valid and match the expected format. The package provides `shellcheck`, conflicts with alternative versions, and follows typical AUR packaging conventions without any signs of malicious injection or supply-chain attacks.
</details>
